To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. # Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Overall:** Reject the package as drafted. Several Seller positions are described as "addressed", "agreed", "settled" or "adequate", but the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts them. Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses and DD-006 are examples. I have treated those descriptions as assertions, not facts.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback that needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. None has been given.
- **Recommendation: REJECT and counter at AUD 6,000,000.** Matching a fallback number does not clear it, because authority is absent.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess above it recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** de minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** The thresholds are five times our position, and an "excess only" basket shifts the first AUD 250,000 of loss onto the Buyer.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months (cl 12.3/13). It also proposes that any limitation applies to *all* Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months. 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** No approval exists, and the default would silently extend general limits to Title, fraud and indemnity claims.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties would sit under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** Title is the core of what we are buying, and capping it at 20% over 18 months is not an administrative point.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No carve-out. The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: REJECT and insert an express carve-out. This is non-negotiable.** Under the playbook nobody may waive it, and "any nature" would purport to cover fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room as at 5pm 22 Sept 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2). DL 1.4 also disclaims any admission.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only, against identified warranties.
- **Recommendation: DELETE DL 1.1–1.2 and limit disclosure to the specific items.** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure would empty the warranties of content.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** The Buyer has no claim for any matter known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any qualifier should use named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: DELETE cl 8.3.** It is a blanket, constructive-knowledge bar that would also defeat the specific indemnities we are negotiating for known issues.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Described as "addressed". The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the condition deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- **Facts (DL 2):** No final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m).
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent, plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied, as a Completion condition.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** "Addressed" is contradicted by the Seller's own disclosure. Reasonable endeavours with consent-on-delivery is inadequate for a material customer.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion".
- **Facts (DL 3):** The facility is not repaid and there is no discharge of security.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** A post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval, and neither is offered.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Facts (DL 5):** On-costs (payroll tax, super) are unaddressed.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or as Seller-funded, with an indemnity.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** The funds flow silently excludes these, so the Company would bear them after Completion. "Agreed price mechanics" is an assertion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate".
- **Facts (DL 4):** The AUD 180,000 figure comes from DD-010 and is not bank-verified either way. There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering failure of IP transfer and third-party claims, while keeping the SOW3 cure (cleared payment plus confirmatory assignment).
- **Recommendation: REJECT the narrow scope and broaden it.** The risk is IP ownership, not just a payment. Do not assume the AUD 180,000 is accurate.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- **Facts (DL 6):** About 1,240 records may be involved. Access, scope and any notification duty are all unknown.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, a completed investigation, regular updates before Completion, and appropriate warranty/indemnity cover.
- **Recommendation: Do not accept the materiality characterisation. Require preservation, investigation and updating covenants.** No confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure should be assumed either way.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total), described as ordinary-course costs.
- **Facts (DL 8):** The disclosure does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:** Diligence on timing, terms and accrual. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation: HOLD pending assessment.** The "ordinary course" label is unverified, but we should not reflexively treat the renewals as Debt.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** The proposal that "any limitation applies to all Claims" (cl 12.3/13) and the "all Claims of any nature" wording would collapse Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes for each category, with no hidden override from the general regime.
- **Recommendation: REJECT and add express carve-outs plus an order-of-precedence clause.** These provisions are a general override.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Facts (DL 10):** The Seller concedes this is a source relied on, not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. This means ASIC searches, PPSR searches, the share certificates, board/shareholder approvals, and confirmation of no options or rights over shares.
- **Recommendation: REJECT DD-012 as sufficient.** An internal register supplied by the Seller is not independent proof. This also ties to the Riverlark security in SPA-N-009.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Says tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** These terms treated as OPEN, with no assumption of unlimited liability and no assumption of resolution.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the "settled" characterisation and keep both terms open for negotiation.** Nothing in our authority process records agreement, and calling them settled would place them under the 20%/18-month regime.

---

### Escalation / authority notes
- **No fallback is unlocked.** Amelia Frost's written authority has not been given for 20%/AUD 4.8m (N-001), 18 months (N-003) or a post-Completion Riverlark release (N-009). Do not concede any of these in the mark-up.
- **Fraud (N-005)** cannot be traded under any authority.
- **Due diligence to refresh before responding:**
  - Bluefen consent status
  - Riverlark payout figure
  - Ironquay payment evidence
  - DD-006 investigation status
  - Sandbar contract terms
  - Independent title searches
- **No action needed on lease and Mossvale (DL 7, 9).** The disclosure does not show consent is triggered by a share sale. We should still confirm that the DD-007 notification is handled at Completion.
